rows.basis: The FY2025 release says nVent 'expanded capacity in several facilities to support data center and power utility growth' but gives no amount or share, and the expansion also serves utilities. The total capex of 93.3M is not attributed. The PP&E increases (buildings +42.9M, machinery +85.5M, CIP +18.5M) are not tied to data centers by category.
No statement links FY2022 capex (40.5M) to data-center or AI capacity.
No statement links FY2023 capex (65.6M) to data-center or AI capacity.
No statement links FY2024 capex (74.0M) to data-center or AI capacity.

The Q2 2026 release announces 'another manufacturing expansion for liquid cooling to meet continued data center demand' with no amount, location or timing. This is a data-center capacity project in words only. Data center, not AI.
No segment cost line or statement attributes opex to data centers or AI.
No segment cost line or statement attributes opex to data centers or AI.
No segment cost line or statement attributes opex to data centers or AI.
No segment cost line or statement attributes opex (852.3M) to data centers or AI.

The FY2025 MD&A says AI-driven growth came through the infrastructure vertical, 'which includes our data centers business that is primarily in our Systems Protection segment'. It credits infrastructure with about 16 points of organic growth, including price. Systems Protection revenue (2,592.9M) is data-center heavy but is not a data-center line, so it is not summed. No data-center dollar figure is stated; the 'over $2B of 2026 data-center sales' figure is call coverage, not release or filing. Data center, not AI.
No statement in the pack links FY2022 revenue to data centers or AI. The Enclosures segment (1,503.7M) is not a data-center line.
No statement in the pack links FY2023 revenue to data centers or AI. The Enclosures segment (1,605.9M) is not a data-center line.
No statement in the pack links FY2024 revenue to data centers or AI. The Systems Protection/Enclosures segment (1,823.3M) is not a data-center line.
The Q2 2025 release raised full-year sales guidance citing 'increasing momentum in data centers and power utilities'. No data-center figure is given. Data center, not AI.

Several releases name data centers as the lead growth driver for 2026 ('led by the infrastructure vertical, particularly data centers'), and the Q1 and Q2 2026 releases cite 'broad-based data center growth' and new products adding over 30 points of growth. None gives a data-center sales figure or share; the over-$2B and $2.5B backlog figures are call, not release or filing. Data center, not AI.
The Q1 2026 release cites 'significant momentum in data centers' in raising guidance, with no figure. Data center, not AI.
